_comment: Demo fixture: a small clinical-decision branching scenario. Two paths from the start node lead to different outcomes.
title: Triage: chest pain

nodes.prompt: A 58-year-old patient walks into the clinic complaining of squeezing chest pain that started 30 minutes ago. What do you do first?

choices.text: Take vitals (BP, HR, SpO₂) and start a focused history.
choices.feedback: Good call — establishing a baseline is the right first move.

choices.text: Reassure them it's likely indigestion and send them home.
choices.feedback: Chest pain in this age group must be evaluated, not dismissed.

nodes.prompt: BP 152/96, HR 102, SpO₂ 96%. Patient is diaphoretic. What's the next step?

choices.text: Order a 12-lead EKG and trend troponin.
choices.feedback: Right — rule out ACS before anything else.

choices.text: Wait 30 minutes and reassess without further workup.
choices.feedback: Delay in diagnosing ACS narrows the treatment window.

nodes.prompt: The EKG shows ST-elevation in the inferior leads. The team activates the cath lab.

outcome.message: Excellent workup. The patient was diagnosed with an inferior STEMI and went to the cath lab within the 90-minute door-to-balloon window.

nodes.prompt: The patient returns 90 minutes later by ambulance in cardiogenic shock.

outcome.message: Adverse outcome. The treatment window was missed. Review the decision points and try again.
